newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes falter on fundamental pressures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes falter on fundamental pressures.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf remained stagnant Monday afternoon in rangebound trading, while grade differentials talked at steady to weaker levels.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was slightly weaker than midday at $18.85-18.95 a barrel, maintaining a 20 cents advantage to July NYMEX futures at $18.65-75 a barrel.
Outright paper prices were pressured by technical weakness and follow-through selling after the widespread NYMEX sell-off Friday brought spot crude prices below $19.00 a barrel.
Domestic grade business focused on a couple of trades in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market, where deals were confirmed at 25 and 24 cents below cash benchmark.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was pegged at 65-75 cents under the marker, and Midland/WTI steady at WTI/Cushing -40 cents, with no new deals to report.
LLS came under renewed oversea pressure, as Dated North Sea Brent declined 12 cents for a July 17-19 loader at July Brent -62 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland held steady, selling at WTI/Cushing -$1.71, and Eugene Island slipped further to move at $2.05 under benchmark.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus were around $1.75-80, with little in the way of fundamental or political happenings moving traders to act.
